lawyer:
MA Hannan, with SM Moniruzzaman, DAG—For Petitioner
Khairun Nessa, AAG—For the Respondents.
parties:
Bangladesh National Insurance Company Ltd ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Commissioner, Customs Excise & VAT, Dhaka (South) and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
7. At the very outset, Mr. MA Hannan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the notice for demand was issued under section 55 of the VAT Act, and, as such, the fine as well as additional tax cannot be imposed on the petitioner under sections 37(2) and 37(3) of the Value Added Tax Act, 1991 and, as such, the impugned demand notice and the adjudicating order issued by Respondent No.2 are liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority having no legal effect. He next submits that after issuance of the notice under section 55 of the VAT Act, the petitioner paid all the VAT amount to the concerned authority, which are evident from the annexures contained in Annexures- C, C1, C2 and C3 and, as such, the question of imposition of fine and additional tax does not arise, and in that view of the matter, the Rule should be made absolute setting aside the impugned demand notice and the adjudicating order allegedly issued by Respondent No. 2. He then submits that the demand for VAT was asked for the period from July, 1998 to 8-4-2000 and the notice contained in Annexure-B was issued on 7-4-2003, and, as such, it appears that the demand for the unpaid VAT was not made within the stipulated period as mentioned in section 55 of the VAT Act, and, as such, the alleged demand notice and the adjudicating order allegedly issued by Respondent No. 2 are also barred by limitation, and, as such, considering that aspect of the case, the Rule should be made absolute setting aside the impugned demand notice and the adjudicating order. He further submits that though there is a forum for preferring appeal against the demand notice and the adjudicating order passed by Respondent No.2, but even in that case, the writ petition is maintainable before this Court as the question of interpretation of law requires and the palpable illegality is there in the impugned order and in the demand notice that were issued by Respondent No.2. He vigorously submits that considering the legal aspects of the case, the writ petitioner without preferring the appeal under section 42 of the VAT Act is very much maintainable in the eye of law. Learned Advocate, in support of his submissions, has referred to a number of decisions in the cases of M/s Chittagong Engineering & Electric Supply Co. Ltd. vs Income Tax Office, reported in 22 DLR (SC) 443, MA Hai vs Trading Corporation of Bangladesh reported in 40 DLR (AD) 206, Dhaka Warehouse Ltd. vs Assistant Collector of Customs reported in 11 BLD (AD) 227, Bangladesh vs Mizanur Rahman reported in 20 BLD (AD) 212. 

 20. The another aspects of the case, is that Respondent No. 2 issued the demand notice asking for VAT for the period from July 1998 to 8-4-2000 and the said notice contained in annexure-B was issued on 7-4-2003, and, as such, it appears that the demand for the unpaid VAT was not made within the stipulated period as mentioned in section 55 of the Value Added Tax Act, 1991 and considering this aspects of the case, we find that the alleged demand notice and the adjudicating order issued by Respondent No.2 are barred by limitation. We have further noticed that the impugned demand notice is the admixture of section 55 and sections 37(2) and 37(3) of the Value Added Tax Act, 1991, which are also not permitted by law.
